source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: The night before cancer surgery, a client says, 'I'm not having surgery. I don't have cancer.' Which defense mechanism is this?
questions.rationale: Denial blocks out painful or anxiety-provoking events to protect the ego.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q916 (PDF p. 1159)
questions.quote: Denial is the defense mechanism that blocks out painful or anxiety-inducing events

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An occupational health nurse learns of a large layoff in 2 weeks. What should she do FIRST to prepare?
questions.rationale: Identifying available services gives immediate avenues for help when the layoff occurs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q917 (PDF p. 1160)
questions.quote: the nurse should identify the services that are available to the employees.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client fears not waking up from anesthesia. What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: The therapeutic response encourages the client to express concerns. The others are stereotyped reassurance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q927 (PDF p. 1171)
questions.quote: The therapeutic response to the client is the one that encourages the client to express her or his concerns.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A recently widowed man's tidy home is now in chaos and he smells of alcohol. What should the home nurse say?
options: 'It seems you're having a hard time.'
questions.rationale: Reflection that he seems to be having a difficult time helps him explore and express his feelings.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q928 (PDF p. 1172)
questions.quote: The therapeutic statement is the one that helps the client explore his situation and express his feelings.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says the doctor gave him wrong information on purpose. Which response is therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the information and exploring whether he will talk with the provider directly supports therapeutic communication.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q945 (PDF p. 1190)
questions.quote: Options 2 and 3 attempt to clarify the information to which the client is referring.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why does a client on PERMANENT TPN need psychosocial support?
options: He will no longer eat orally
questions.rationale: Permanent TPN is for clients who can no longer absorb enteral nutrients, so they lose the experience of eating.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q952 (PDF p. 1197)
questions.quote: These clients will no longer take nutrition orally.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client going home with a new colostomy says, 'I don't know how I'll do it alone.' What is BEST?
questions.rationale: The client expresses fear and helplessness; arranging home care support meets this need.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q953 (PDF p. 1198)
questions.quote: The client is expressing feelings of fear and helplessness.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before parathyroidectomy a client says, 'I'll have to wear a scarf after this.' Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: The statement reflects concern about appearance after surgery.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q958 (PDF p. 1205)
questions.quote: The client’s statement reflects a psychosocial concern regarding his or her appearance after surgery

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client treated for thyroid storm is still anxious and labile at discharge. What is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Anxiety and lability are normal after thyroid storm; the nurse helps the client cope with these changes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q960 (PDF p. 1207)
questions.quote: It is normal for clients who experience thyroid storm (hyperthyroidism) to continue to be anxious and emotionally labile

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client who works with the public worries about her new subclavian CVC. Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: A visible CVC can create socially awkward situations and affect body image.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q961 (PDF p. 1208)
questions.quote: The CVC can create socially awkward situations and impair the client’s security in her body image.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A man burned while drunk now needs an amputation and looks upset after signing consent. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Reflection elicits deeper awareness of feelings and validates the nurse's perception.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q965 (PDF p. 1212)
questions.quote: Reflection statements tend to elicit a deeper awareness of feelings.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is a client told to fast and take an enema before peritoneoscopy?
options: To empty and protect the bowel
questions.rationale: A laparoscope is inserted after gas insufflation; an empty bowel reduces the risk of puncture and improves visualization.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q969 (PDF p. 1217)
questions.quote: Abdominal peritoneoscopy is performed to directly visualize the liver, gallbladder, spleen, and stomach

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How should the nurse BEST meet the cultural needs of a child's family from another culture?
questions.rationale: Asking about specific cultural needs and treatments helps the nurse understand the family's beliefs and health practices.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q975 (PDF p. 1224)
questions.quote: it is important to ask questions about their specific cultural needs and means of treatment.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which plan addresses psychosocial needs before an above-knee amputation?
questions.rationale: Loss of a body part alters body image; interventions encourage expressing feelings about the change.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q979 (PDF p. 1228)
questions.quote: Surgical incisions or the loss of a body part can alter a client’s body image.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After consent for an IVC filter, a client says he is scared the procedure will fail. Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: He names the procedure and outcome as the object, which is fear. Anxiety has no identifiable source.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q984 (PDF p. 1233)
questions.quote: Anxiety is present when the client cannot identify the source of the uneasy feelings.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client asks if pulmonary angiography is painful and has much radiation. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Pulmonary angiography involves minimal radiation and is painless except for discomfort at needle insertion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q986 (PDF p. 1235)
questions.quote: Pulmonary angiography involves minimal exposure to radiation.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client scheduled for a stress test says he is nervous. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: An open-ended response explores feelings and builds trust.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q989 (PDF p. 1239)
questions.quote: The nurse should explore a client’s feelings if concerns are expressed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client is anxious that his infiltrated IV must be removed. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Acknowledging the anxiety and honestly saying the IV may be restarted is giving information therapeutically.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q993 (PDF p. 1243)
questions.quote: The correct option addresses the client’s anxiety and honestly informs the client that the IV may need to be restarted.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with AKI has trouble remembering instructions. How should the nurse communicate?
questions.rationale: Communication should be clear, simple, and understandable, repeated as needed, because of anxiety and altered lab values.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1001 (PDF p. 1252)
questions.quote: Communications should be clear, simple, and understandable.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A CABG client and spouse argue after rehab. What is BEST for the nurse to say?
questions.rationale: Acknowledging feelings without inserting values or judgment keeps communication open.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1002 (PDF p. 1253)
questions.quote: Acknowledging the client’s feelings without inserting your own values or judgments is a method of therapeutic communication.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A first-time inpatient with a roommate cannot start urinating. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Lack of privacy inhibits voiding. Privacy, running water, and normal position help.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1006 (PDF p. 1257)
questions.quote: A lack of privacy is a key issue that may inhibit the ability of the client to void

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client living alone fears complications after outpatient surgery. Which response uses reflection?
questions.rationale: Reflection directs the client's feelings back. The others give false reassurance or minimize.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1007 (PDF p. 1258)
questions.quote: In option 4, the nurse uses reflection to direct the client’s feelings and concerns.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which communication method is BEST for a client with an endotracheal tube?
questions.rationale: An intubated client cannot speak; a picture or word board is simplest and needs least energy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1009 (PDF p. 1260)
questions.quote: The use of a picture or word board is the simplest method of communication

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on home TPN says she misses eating dinner with her family. What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Clarifying and focusing help the client explore concerns about her treatment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1010 (PDF p. 1261)
questions.quote: The nurse assists the client with expressing feelings and dealing with the aspects of illness and treatment

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client fears thoracentesis. Which honest information supports her?
questions.rationale: Needle insertion is painful; staying still prevents injury to the pleura and lung.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1012 (PDF p. 1263)
questions.quote: The needle insertion for thoracentesis is painful for the client.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A daughter says, 'If this is a stroke, it's the kiss of death.' What should the nurse say FIRST?
questions.rationale: Restating lets the daughter verbalize feelings and begin coping.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1019 (PDF p. 1292)
questions.quote: Option 2 allows the daughter to verbalize her feelings, begin coping, and adapt to what is happening.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: What is the MOST immediate concern when planning care for a group of homeless people?
questions.rationale: The first community health concern is always basic physiological needs: food, shelter, and clothing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1023 (PDF p. 1296)
questions.quote: The initial community health concern is always attending to people’s basic physiological needs of food, shelter, and clothing.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: An older couple's home was flooded. What does the community health nurse plan FIRST?
questions.rationale: Initial disaster concerns are basic physiological needs: food, shelter, and clothing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1027 (PDF p. 1300)
questions.quote: The initial concerns of community health are always attending to people’s

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A partner says, 'I thought the tube the first time would make him quit drinking.' What is BEST?
options: 'You hoped this would make him stop?'
questions.rationale: Clarifying and focusing help the partner express feelings about the chronic illness.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1032 (PDF p. 1306)
questions.quote: the nurse uses the therapeutic communication techniques of clarifying and focusing

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before discharge after HHS, a client voices worry about managing diabetes. What should the new nurse do?
options: Suggest she move in with family
questions.rationale: Provide time, listen to concerns, and clarify feelings.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1033 (PDF p. 1307)
questions.quote: The nurse should provide time and listen to the client’s concerns while attempting to clarify the client’s feelings

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should staff speak to a hearing-impaired client?
questions.rationale: Face the client and speak clearly in a normal tone; do not shout.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1035 (PDF p. 1309)
questions.quote: the caregiver should speak in a normal tone to the client and should not shout.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client wants help to live independently. Which communication action has HIGHEST priority?
questions.rationale: Active listening and noting verbal and nonverbal cues receive the intended message and build comfort.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1036 (PDF p. 1310)
questions.quote: the nurse uses active listening and assesses for verbal and nonverbal communication

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An anxious client with angina asks, 'So I had a heart attack?' What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: The nurse corrects the misconception: angina results from inadequate blood supply causing pain, without infarction.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1039 (PDF p. 1313)
questions.quote: Angina pectoris occurs as a result of an inadequate blood supply to the myocardium causing pain

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which question BEST assesses adjustment to a new CAD diagnosis?
options: 'How do you feel about this diagnosis?'
questions.rationale: Exploring feelings helps determine adjustment and individualize care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1041 (PDF p. 1315)
questions.quote: Exploring feelings assists the nurse with determining the individualized plan of care

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on crutches says, 'I'll always be crippled.' What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Clarification and validation deal with the problem from the client's perspective.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1042 (PDF p. 1316)
questions.quote: The correct option demonstrates the therapeutic communication technique of clarification and validation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After hip repair, a client keeps refusing to walk. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: An open-ended question explores factors behind the refusal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1044 (PDF p. 1318)
questions.quote: many different factors may be contributing to the client’s refusal to ambulate as prescribed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which technique encourages a paranoid client who fears poisoned food to share his fears?
questions.rationale: Open-ended questions and silence encourage descriptive discussion of feelings.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1046 (PDF p. 1320)
questions.quote: Open-ended questions and silence are strategies that are used to encourage clients to discuss their feelings

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A family member says ECT won't help and causes memory loss. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Seeking data about what they know helps clarify information and address concerns.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1047 (PDF p. 1321)
questions.quote: the nurse is looking for data to assist with clarifying information about the procedure with the family
